title: Three Seasons and One Short Mat
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：high　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 high 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the jumper ① set the high that no rival in the stadium would have measured, and he said the setting was the whole of the season. The ② high, meaning the mark itself and not the mat, ran three seasons and stayed unmeasured in the book; a high, he said, is the only thing in a stadium that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ high in that stadium had the same short mat beside it, and the ④ high at the far stand, meaning the best they kept for the children to aim at and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A high, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the jumper said the measuring is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the high was the whole of the matter, meaning the level and not the mark. The ⑥ high, meaning the level and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; high, he said, is either something you set or the only word that means both a mark and a level. He said the level is the part they remember.

By 1994 the ⑦ high had become a line in a board, and the board had become an argument about the short mat. The ⑧ high of the whole thing, the jumper wrote in July, was one stadium and three seasons of measuring; high, he said, is either the best at the far stand or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ high I remember is the mark measured in the board, which closed in 1996 and is still measured as the quietest in the stadium. A ⑩ high, my mother said in 1998, is the only mark that improves by being measured; every high, she said, is a level that has agreed to look like a mark. She said the level was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 最高水平；新高（指体育场里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 最高水平；新高（指那个纪录线本身，与垫子相对）
C. 固定搭配：set the high 创下新高
D. n. 最高水平；新高（指留给孩子们学着冲击的那一个）
E. n. 新高之事（抽象总称，指一处体育场的新高之事）
F. n. 最高水平；新高（指记分牌里写到、被量过的的那一个）
G. n. 水准、层次（指一件事里人人都跳却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: set the high that no rival in the stadium would have measured

answers.why: set the high 意为“创下新高”，1989 年那位跳高运动员把体育场里没有一位对手肯丈量的一个新高水平做了一遍。
high 意为“最高水平；新高”，指那个纪录线本身而不是垫子，它经过了三个赛季而在簿子上没有被丈量。
high 意为“最高水平；新高”，指体育场里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一块薄薄的垫子。
high 意为“最高水平；新高”，指最远那排看台留给孩子们学着冲击的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
high 意为“水准、层次”，指一件事里人人都跳却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个水准就是那件事的全部。
high 意为“层次”，指人人都跳却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个纪录线，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
high 意为“最高水平；新高”，指记分牌里写到、被量过的的那一个，到 1994 年这一个成了记分牌里的一行。
high 意为“新高之事”，跳高运动员七月写道，整件事的新高之事是一处体育场和三个赛季的丈量。
high 意为“最高水平；新高”，我记得的是记分牌里丈量过的那一个，1996 年刷新了，至今仍被说成体育场里最安静的一个。
high 为抽象总称，母亲 1998 年说，新高是唯一会因为被好好丈量而变得更好的纪录线。
